title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat and dark‑green vegetables, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs, lean meat (such as chicken breast or turkey) and dark‑green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, kale). No fat is added – it is cooked on a dry pan or in the microwave. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, meat adds extra protein and iron, and the greens supply vitamins, minerals and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most nutrient‑dense foods, containing all essential amino acids.
Dark‑green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, which may support body detoxification.
Cooking without added fat preserves the natural taste of the ingredients and lowers the calorie count.
The combination of protein and fiber helps keep you feeling full longer.
The dish is quick to prepare, making it a popular breakfast or light‑lunch option.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Eggs and meat together provide about 25‑30 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle and tissue maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and meat supply vitamin B12, while the greens provide folate (B9), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Lean meat and spinach deliver easily absorbable iron and zinc, which support immune function.

items.title: Antioxidants and phytochemicals
items.content: Dark‑green vegetables contain lutein, zeaxanthin and vitamin K, beneficial for eye health and bone strength.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The absence of added fat keeps the dish light: roughly 250‑300 kcal per serving.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Processed meat concerns
items.content: Choose lean, minimally processed meat to avoid excess sodium and additives.

items.title: Oxalates in spinach
items.content: Large amounts of spinach can increase the risk of kidney stones in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs, add finely chopped meat and pre‑cooked or lightly steamed dark‑green vegetables. Pour the mixture onto a hot dry pan, cook over medium heat, stirring until the desired consistency is reached. Season with pepper, paprika or herbs if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best eaten fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat on a dry pan or in the microwave.
